preface.title: Preface
preface.para: This book describes ooRexx/Python, a native bridge between Open Object Rexx and Python 3 that works both ways. An ooRexx program uses Python modules (the standard library, numpy, pandas, matplotlib, anything installed) as Rexx objects; a Python program creates ooRexx interpreters, runs Rexx code, and uses Rexx objects as Python objects.

This book is a reference rather than a tutorial. It assumes you know ooRexx, and enough Python to read the documentation of the Python modules you want to use. Its companion, ooRexx/Python: Cookbook, introduces the main concepts through short programs that can be run as they are.
Sections that document a concept carry a small example: a complete program, followed by what it prints. Every one of them is run, and its output checked, by the project's tests.

section.title: Related Information
section.para: See also ooRexx and Python: Cookbook, Open Object Rexx: Reference, and the Python documentation at https://docs.python.org/3/. How the bridge is built, and why each choice was made, is in the design document of the project's repository, docs/design.md.
